newsitem.title: USA: ChemTrak completes trials on HIV test.
newsitem.headline: ChemTrak completes trials on HIV test.

text.p: ChemTrak Inc. said it has successfully completed the pre-clinical trials of one-step AWARE Rapid HIV Test and found the results equivalent to the gold standard ELISA and Western Blot test methods.
In a statement, ChemTrak said the Rapid HIV Test brings accurate HIV test results in three to fifteen minutes utilizing a single drop of blood directly from a finger-stick sample.
The pre-clinical trials evaluated 217 clinical specimens providing 100 percent correlation with results obtained from instrument-based ELISA and Western Blot tests.

In four commercially available seroconversion panels, the test detected all the positives with the accuracy of the ELISA and Western Blot tests. The company said the test was found to be highly sensitive by accurately detecting all positives and no cross reactivity was observed with specimens from individuals with non-HIV infections such as Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, syphilis, HTLV-1, HTLV-2 and CMV.
The company anticipates that clinical trials of the HIV Rapid Test will begin in two countries outside the United States during the third quarter 1997.

ChemTrak plans to initiate clinical trials in the U.S. during the fourth quarter 1997 and anticipates filing for U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance for the physicians' office market this year.
